chapters.title: Meeting overview and recap
chapters.gist: The Project Manager introduces the final meeting and summarizes previous design decisions.

chapters.title: Prototype and UI presentation
chapters.gist: The User Interface Designer and Industrial Designer present the physical model and its interface features.

chapters.title: Budget review and adjustments
chapters.gist: The team evaluates costs and decides to remove the LCD screen to stay under budget.

chapters.title: Design evaluation session
chapters.gist: The Marketing Expert leads a scoring exercise to see how well the design meets original project goals.

chapters.title: Process and teamwork feedback
chapters.gist: Team members share their opinions on project leadership, communication, and creative constraints.

chapters.title: Discussion on modeling tools
chapters.gist: The Industrial Designer explains how using Play-Doh helped the tangible creative process.

chapters.title: Meeting conclusion
chapters.gist: The Project Manager confirms all items are addressed and concludes the meeting.

action_items.text: Specify the final design details in the final report.
Submit the results of the design evaluation criteria.
Complete and write the final project report.

content.tldr: The project team met to finalize the detailed design of a TV remote and evaluate the overall project success. They adjusted the design to meet budget constraints and provided feedback on the collaboration process.

bullets.text: Finalize the look and feel and user interface design for the remote control.
Evaluate the final product against the original project requirements.
The team removed the LCD screen and advanced chip to save four point three Euro.
The final design scored approximately seventy percent efficacy against original goals.
Modeling materials like Play-Doh were highly valued for their tangible help in design.
Final physical dimensions and component colors.
Detailed cost breakdown using an Excel budget sheet.
Critique of leadership and the institutional nature of the meeting room.
The Project Manager will write the final specification report.

content.tldr: The team successfully finalized the remote design and ensured it stays within the sixteen Euro budget. The project reached about seventy-two percent of its original design goals.

bullets.text: The team presented a ten-centimeter tall snowman-shaped prototype.
A jog-dial and number pad were integrated into the final interface.
The project was initially four point three Euro over the target budget.
Technological gear in the meeting room felt restrictive to creative communication.
The team removed the LCD screen and the advanced chip to reduce costs.
The remote will use plastic buttons instead of rubber to save money.
The device will be powered by batteries rather than kinetic power.
The Project Manager must document all final specs in the final project report.

content.tldr: The team has finished the prototype and is now performing a final evaluation to close the project. Budget adjustments were completed to ensure financial compliance.

bullets.text: The designers created a physical prototype nicknamed Ninja Homer.
The team finalized the set of advanced functions like brightness and contrast.
Finalize the cost list to stay under the budget limit.
Evaluate team leadership, creativity, and collaboration effectiveness.
Costs for special colors and components were too high for the original design.

content.tldr: While the project successfully produced a budget-compliant design, the team felt that rigid structures and technical equipment hindered their creative potential. They suggested more informal communication in the future.

bullets.text: Using Play-Doh helped the team understand dimensions and engage their senses.
Decisions were made through a consensus system that everyone accepted.
The digital pens and technical gear felt clunky and distracting.
Strict time limits and meeting structures felt disempowering to team members.
Restricting communication to only formal meetings slowed down progress.
Allow team members to communicate and collaborate outside of scheduled meetings.
Use a shared fifth computer in the room to avoid constant cable switching.
Introduce prototypes earlier in the design process to align mental models.

content.tldr: This meeting focused on internal design and project evaluation; no sales to external clients or prospects occurred.

bullets.text: No prospect needs were discussed.
No sales objections were raised.
The internal production budget was limited to twelve and a half Euro.
No sales-related next steps were identified.

content.tldr: The meeting was a group project wrap-up rather than a one-on-one session. Team-wide feedback was gathered regarding leadership and process.

bullets.text: The group felt the atmosphere during meetings was generally relaxed.
The Marketing Expert felt the room and gear created boundaries to creativity.
The Project Manager's leadership was described as strong but potentially confining.
No individual performance follow-ups were assigned.
